calibration.reference_10: Seeing Theory (Brown University), e.g. its 'Probability Distributions' and 'Sampling Distribution' chapters — one continuous manipulable model where the visual encoding itself carries the idea.
calibration.reference_8: BBC Bitesize GCSE Maths 'Analysing data' interactive revision pages (with Khan Academy's AP Statistics study-design unit as the exercise-set equivalent): correct, classroom-ready, accessible, but exercise-and-response rather than a manipulable model.

verdict: A polished, statistically sound investigation: every learner-facing number matches the bundled data, each activity is a real experiment with a gate that forces exploration, and the nuance (non-zero axis ≠ deception; bias ≠ size; association ≠ causation) is taught explicitly. Two defects keep it below the 8 bar: the educator guide's sampling paragraph quotes ranges the bundled data do not support, and the case-file wording check can flag the lesson's own careful 'never proves' phrasing as over-claiming. Fix both and this is an 8.

carry_over.evidence: index.html:106 hint now names the first three tiles as data properties and the 'gap as drawn' fourth tile as deliberately a picture property (the same 1.8-point gap against the chosen axis); app.js:158-162 renders exactly those four tiles, the fourth being the only one that moves. The false universal is gone.

app.js:205-208 'Too relaxed.' branch now computes tallest from state.a1.rangesSeen and quotes fmt(tallest) and the real ratio; apparentGapPct is 1.8 / 9 / 45 for 0–100 / 60–80 / 70–74, so a learner who tried only 0–100 and 60–80 is told about 5×, not 25×. The stale '25×' wording survives only in EDUCATOR_GUIDE.md:26 (see non_blocking).

blocking.issue: The educator guide's sampling paragraph quotes ranges the bundled data do not support: at n = 10 convenience draws scatter from about 10–90% late-library (not 'roughly 55–68%') and can sit above the population mean, so 'their mean sleep sits about 0.4–0.65 h low regardless of size' is false as written for sizes the learner is offered.
blocking.why_it_caps_score: A statistics educator cannot sign off on a teacher guide whose numbers disagree with the bundled data (bar test fails).
blocking.fix: Replace the sentence 'The table makes the mechanism visible: … while random draws wobble at n=10 and converge by n=500.' with: "The table makes the mechanism visible: convenience draws land near the library-door share of 57.4% late-library users (against the true 25.2%) with a mean sleep about 0.4 h below the population's 7.30 h at every size — 300 seeded draws at n = 500 run roughly 53–63% late-library and 0.30–0.49 h low, while n = 10 draws scatter widely (about 10–90% late-library; means from about 0.8 h above to 1.3 h below the truth). The shortfall does not shrink as n grows; random draws wobble at n = 10 and converge by n = 500."

blocking.issue: The case-file wording check flags the lesson's own cautious phrasing as over-claiming: 'never'/'always' and any 'proves' match even inside negated statements, so a learner who writes 'correlation never proves a cause' — the exact habit the lesson teaches — is told their wording claims too much.
blocking.why_it_caps_score: Learner-facing feedback that names a misconception the learner does not have fails the 'specific feedback' bar for an 8.

non_blocking.issue: The guide still describes the a1 'never' counter-example as 'the 25× taller gap'; after the R2-ED-2 fix the app quotes the gap's share of the axis height at the learner's own widest zoom (about 5× if they only tried 60–80).
non_blocking.fix: Change '…both extremes get specific counter-examples (a hospital temperature chart; the 25× taller gap).' to '…both extremes get specific counter-examples (a hospital temperature chart; the gap's share of the axis height at their widest zoom, up to 25× taller at 70–74).'

non_blocking.issue: The start screen promises 'a headline that fails all three on purpose', but the builder accepts at least two of the three tricks (which is what the bounty brief asks for).
non_blocking.fix: Change index.html:46 to '…and you'll finish by writing a headline that fails at least two of the three on purpose.'

non_blocking.issue: The a1 notebook note hard-codes '(1.8% of the axis height at 0–100 vs 45.0% at 70–74)' instead of the ranges the learner actually tried — the same defect class R2-ED-2 fixed in the feedback.

The case-file evidence heuristic accepts words belonging to the other activities ('axis', 'mean', 'sample') as an observation about the Port Lumen headline, so a learner citing the wrong screen can be told their observation 'points at something concrete in the data'.

keep: The a1 statistics box: three invariant tiles (means, final-term difference) plus the deliberately dynamic 'gap as drawn (share of the axis height)' tile — the picture/data distinction is manipulable, numbered, and correctly named by the hint.

The a1 reflect step: a three-way choice whose accepted answer is 'it depends', with a hospital-temperature counter-example for 'always' and a computed counter for 'never' — scrutiny taught, not blanket distrust.

The a2 design: population truths shown up front, a dashed population line on the chart, and a table whose 'vs population' columns make bias visible — gated so the question cannot be answered until one sample of each method exists.

The a3 investigation sequence: r defined before the first statistic appears, season colouring → within-season r, and a check that refuses the keyed answer until the learner has seen the within-season values.

The headline builder (≥2 tricks + caption naming them) and the next-practice box ('a chart can pass all three and still be wrong — and fail one and still be honest. Scrutiny, not blanket distrust.') — genuine transfer tasks.
gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown): each chapter is one continuous manipulable model where the visual encoding is the concept — distributions reshape under the cursor, sampling distributions build as you watch — so the idea is felt, not ticked. Data Detective is correct, gated and well-feedbacked, but each activity varies a single axis with the statistics in a separate box; at 10 the chart, the numbers and the misconception would be one surface, and the sampling activity would show the bias accumulating live rather than plotting dots beside a dashed line.
